questions.question: How do you review your code in the age of AI?
questions.answer_summary: Traditional review criteria (readability, maintainability, correctness) are proving insufficient because AI-generated code often 'works' but follows logic that is unfamiliar or subtly incorrect, forcing reviewers to change what they look for.

questions.question: What tools are people using for human review of AI-assisted code?
questions.answer_summary: AI review tools like CodeRabbit and Copilot catch bugs and style issues well but are weaker at spotting duplicate code, cross-module coupling, and separation-of-concerns problems, so human review is still needed for architecture-level issues.

questions.question: Is anyone else sick of AI-generated ('splattered') code flooding reviews?
questions.answer_summary: A consultant reported observing at least 8 companies embracing AI-generated code for coding, testing, and reviews without matching review rigor, causing visible quality decline.

questions.question: Should the author of AI-generated code also be its reviewer?
questions.answer_summary: The community debate centers on whether self-review by the prompter is sufficient given the author didn't actually write the logic being reviewed.

questions.question: Is there an 'AI code review bubble' of low-value tooling?
questions.answer_summary: Commenters argue a good reviewer (human or AI) should focus on functional correctness rather than getting lost in minor style/naming nits, which is where many AI review tools currently add noise.

questions.question: Why is the 'generate and submit' pattern destroying code quality?
questions.answer_summary: Developers enable agent mode, generate large diffs unsupervised, and submit minimal-description PRs; reviewers then discover inconsistent patterns, missing error handling, and security gaps, turning review into an audit of AI output rather than a discussion of the author's understanding.

questions.question: Does AI-generated code need its own AI reviewer?
questions.answer_summary: As AI-written code volume grows, teams are adding AI review platforms as an automated 'senior engineer' layer for security, race conditions, and performance, shifting human developers toward an editor/validator role rather than original author.

questions.question: Who is responsible when AI-generated code breaks production?
questions.answer_summary: The framing that emerges is that submitting a PR is still a claim that 'I believe this is production-ready' — accountability doesn't transfer to the AI tool.

questions.question: Does AI-generated code require more review rounds than human-written code?
questions.answer_summary: Comparative research found human reviewers exchange 11.8% more rounds of back-and-forth when reviewing AI-generated code versus human-written code.

questions.question: Are AI reviewer suggestions actually adopted into codebases?
questions.answer_summary: AI agent review suggestions get adopted at a much lower rate than human reviewer suggestions (16.6% vs 56.5%), with over half of unadopted AI suggestions being incorrect or handled differently.

questions.question: Does relying on AI coding tools reduce what developers actually learn?
questions.answer_summary: A 2026 study found developers using AI finished tasks slightly faster but scored only 50% on post-task knowledge assessments versus 67% for a control group without AI, raising concerns about long-term skill and code-ownership erosion that review processes must now account for.

questions.question: What's the best AI code review tool right now?
questions.answer_summary: Community discussion points to tools like Kodus, CodeRabbit, and Qodo Merge, which learn from a team's existing review patterns rather than applying generic checks.

questions.question: Is code review's real purpose bug-finding or knowledge-sharing, and how does AI change that?
questions.answer_summary: Practitioners note code review's core purpose has always been knowledge-sharing and education more than bug-finding, and AI-generated code disrupts this because there's no author to learn from or question about intent.

questions.question: Are junior developers treating AI coding tools as 'magic wands' and how does that affect reviewers?
questions.answer_summary: Junior/mid-level engineers are increasingly treating AI output as inherently correct ('the AI is smarter than me'), which pushes more verification burden onto senior reviewers and increases review fatigue.
